user:
Write the task-facing text for a service-level-agreement audit task at a fictional cloud provider. Agents audit customer contracts for one reporting month. They read each customer's contract (numbered clauses), the customer's subscriptions (instances: instance id, service, region), a shared incident log (incident id, start and end in UTC, service, region, scope = either "region-wide" or a list of instance ids, impact = outage or degraded, cause = platform, network, maintenance, upstream_provider, force_majeure or customer_action, "caused by" = the tenant or customer id for customer_action, notice id for maintenance), maintenance notices (sent time, planned start and planned end in UTC), support tickets (priority P1, P2 or P3, opened time and first-response time in UTC) and service-credit claims (month claimed, filing date).

Code fills ids, numbers and dates into your sentences through {placeholders}, and a parser reads the filled sentences back, so: keep every placeholder exactly as named, use each listed placeholder exactly once in each template, keep each template on a single line, never use the character "|", and do not write any digits yourself (write "P1", "P2", "P3" for priorities; spell out business hours in words: Monday to Friday, nine in the morning to five in the afternoon). Placeholders are filled with bare numbers, so write the unit after them yourself (for example "{target}%" or "{hours} hours"). Return one JSON object with these keys:

"company": a fictional cloud provider name (2-3 words).
"intro": the opening paragraph of the task prompt. Placeholders {company}, {n}, {first}, {last}, {month}. Say that the service-assurance team of {company} must audit the {n} customer contracts {first} to {last} for the reporting month {month}: for every customer decide whether the availability commitment and the support response commitment were breached, compute the customer's measured availability for the month, and determine the service credit owed.
"rule_scope": a paragraph without placeholders: each customer has the instances listed in its subscriptions; an incident affects a customer when its scope lists one of the customer's instance ids, or when its scope is region-wide and it is on a service in a region where the customer has an instance of that service; incidents on other instances never affect the customer, even on the same service and region.
"rule_measure": a paragraph without placeholders: all times are UTC; the reporting month runs from the first day at midnight to the first day of the next month at midnight; availability = one hundred times (minutes in the month minus downtime minutes) divided by minutes in the month; only the part of an incident inside the month counts, but any minimum-length rule looks at the incident's whole logged duration from start to end; outage minutes count in full and degraded minutes count by the contract's degradation weight; when incidents overlap, each minute counts once, with the heaviest weight that applies to it; which causes are excluded is set by the customer's contract; for maintenance that meets the contract's notice and window conditions only the minutes between the notice's planned start and planned end are excluded, and any minutes of that incident outside the planned period count as downtime; maintenance that does not meet the conditions counts in full; report availability as a percentage rounded to three decimals.
"rule_support": a paragraph without placeholders: only tickets opened inside the reporting month count, even when they are answered after it, and tickets opened before the month do not count; P1 response time is measured in calendar minutes from opening to first response; P2 and P3 response times are measured in business hours, Monday to Friday from nine in the morning to five in the afternoon in the customer's timezone shown in the contract (a fixed UTC offset with no daylight saving), and the clock does not run outside business hours; a ticket misses its target only when its response time is strictly greater than the target; the support commitment is breached when at least one counted ticket misses its target.
"rule_credit": a paragraph without placeholders: the availability commitment is breached when the availability is strictly below the committed target; the availability credit is the credit of the lowest threshold that the availability falls below; if the support commitment is breached the contract's support credit is added once; the total is limited by the contract's cap; a credit is owed only if the customer filed a claim for this reporting month on or before the claim deadline, counted in days after the last day of the month (filing on the deadline day is in time), and a claim for a different month does not count; without a valid claim the credit is zero, but the breaches are still reported.
"answer_line": one paragraph with placeholder {example}: the final answer must be one JSON object keyed by customer id; each value has "breaches" (a list containing "availability" and/or "support", empty if neither was breached), "availability" (the percentage with three decimals) and "credit" (the credit owed as a percentage of the monthly fee, a number); then show {example} as the format example.
"unit_prompt": placeholders {customer} and {month}: a short instruction to audit only customer {customer} for the reporting month {month} with the same rules and tools, and to answer with a JSON object that has only that customer's key.

Contract clauses: each of the following keys is a list of exactly three differently worded variants of one contract clause (formal contract language, one sentence or two, single line each). Each variant must state the same facts:
"c_target": placeholder {target}: the provider commits to a monthly availability of at least {target}% for the subscribed instances.
"c_deg_full": no placeholder: minutes of degraded service count in full as downtime, like an outage.
"c_deg_half": no placeholder: each minute of degraded service counts as half a minute of downtime.
"c_deg_none": no placeholder: degraded service is not downtime; only outages count.
"c_minlen": placeholder {minutes}: an incident whose logged duration is shorter than {minutes} minutes is not counted as downtime; an incident lasting exactly that long or longer counts.
"c_minlen_none": no placeholder: every incident counts as downtime regardless of how short it is.
"c_maint": placeholders {hours} and {window}: scheduled maintenance is excluded from downtime only when its notice was sent at least {hours} hours before the planned start and the whole planned period lies within the weekly maintenance window {window}; other maintenance counts as downtime.
"c_upstream_counts": no placeholder: failures of upstream providers count as downtime.
"c_upstream_excluded": no placeholder: failures of upstream providers are excluded from downtime.
"c_force_majeure": no placeholder: incidents caused by force majeure are excluded from downtime.
"c_customer_action": no placeholder: incidents caused by the customer's own actions are excluded from downtime; incidents caused by other tenants are not excluded.
"c_support": placeholders {p1}, {p2}, {p3}: first response within {p1} minutes for P1 tickets around the clock, within {p2} business hours for P2 tickets and within {p3} business hours for P3 tickets.
"c_support_credit": placeholder {support_credit}: if any ticket misses its response target in the month, the customer receives an additional credit of {support_credit}% of the monthly fee.
"c_tiers": placeholders {t1}, {c1}, {t2}, {c2}, {t3}, {c3}: availability below {t1}% earns a credit of {c1}% of the monthly fee, below {t2}% a credit of {c2}%, and below {t3}% a credit of {c3}%.
"c_cap": placeholder {cap}: total service credits for a month never exceed {cap}% of the monthly fee.
"c_claim": placeholder {days}: credits must be claimed in writing within {days} days after the end of the month to which they apply, otherwise they are forfeited.

"tools": an object with one short description (one or two sentences, no placeholders) for each tool: "list_customers" (customer id, name and contract id; paged with offset and limit), "read_contract" (the full contract of one customer, including its timezone), "get_subscriptions" (a customer's instances with service and region), "search_incidents" (incident log rows filtered by any of service, region, instance_id, start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD; instance_id matches only incidents whose scope lists that instance, so region-wide incidents are found by service and region; paged with offset, forty rows per page), "read_notice" (one maintenance notice by id), "list_tickets" (a customer's support tickets, including any opened outside the month), "list_claims" (a customer's credit claims), "calculator" (evaluates an arithmetic expression).
